trust_decision.summary: The libxml2 parse flags in main/xml.c decide whether external entities in an XML document get expanded: XML_PARSE_NOENT (expand) or XML_PARSE_NONET (no network). At the pinned commit all three xmlRead* calls already use RECOVER|NONET, so the published change is already applied.

landing_point.why: The advisory names xml.c and xmlReadFile with XML_PARSE_NOENT. ast_xml_open is the xmlReadFile call it describes.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is nothing left to dismiss. No NOENT flag remains anywhere in the pinned tree, and the remaining parsers use libxml2 defaults that do not expand entities. A solver could correctly say the code is already safe.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: XInclude processing and the xml-stylesheet processing instruction (PI) when the core XML documentation files load. An over-broad fix that drops XInclude or XSLT would break the documentation loaded through ast_xml_open.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ast_xml_read_memory parses with xmlParseMemory and default options. A copy could re-add NOENT or DTDLOAD here when it moves to xmlReadMemory.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The 20.9.0 changelog says deprecated xmlParseMemory calls were being moved to xmlReadMemory with explicit flags. A maintainer porting this function could copy the old NOENT flag set. This function parses network-supplied SIP PIDF-LO bodies (res/res_pjsip_geolocation.c:330, channels/chan_sip.c:28225), so the sibling would sit in another package (res/, channels/) from the landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The xmlReaderForMemory call over a CalDAV server response passes options 0. A sibling copy could pass XML_PARSE_NOENT there.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is a separate libxml2 consumer outside main/xml.c (a second implementation at distance) that parses remote server data. Setting NOENT so that entity text arrives substituted is a plausible convenience edit.

O10_build.toolchain: autoconf ./configure + GNU make, gcc; libxml2, optional libxslt
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_xml_escape.c covers only XML escaping. The geolocation unit test parses an embedded PIDF via ast_xml_read_memory (res/res_geolocation/geoloc_eprofile.c:1532). No test covers parser flags or entities.
